newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - April 8.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday:
* The Nasdaq composite index closed up 14.62 points at 1,251.35, led higher by strength in the technology sector.
* Advanced Micro Devices and Motorola reported strong financial results after the market closed.
* Rational Software agreed to acquire rival Pure Atria in a stock swap valued at about $890 million but their shares fell on concerns the companies would cannibalise each others' sales.
* America Online and CompuServe declined to confirm continuing reports AOL was in talks to buy CompuServe and both companies' shares fell.
* The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Pharmacia & Upjohn's new AIDS drug despite conflicting evidence about how well it worked.
* Allegheny Power said it would buy DQE Inc in a $2.6 billion utility deal.
* Consumer debt growth slowed in February, rising at a 6.7 percent seasonally adjusted rate after rising at a 10.3 percent rate in January.
* MESA Inc agreed to merge with Parker & Parsley in a deal which would create the third-largest independent oil and gas exploration and production company in the United States.
* Integrated Health Services backed away from its bid to buy Coram Healthcare.
* Several family members have mounted a legal challenge to Harold Simmons's control of the fortune he reaped as a corporate raider and executive.

* Personal computer industry leaders voiced a vision for television's future and executives outlined the technical format for digital televisions some PC makers plan to include in personal computers. But the format is incompatible with digital technology broadcasters plan to introduce next year.
* The Commerce Department said Commerce Secretary William Daley will head a trade mission to Latin America next month.
* Staples and Office Depot said they would "vigorously contest" a Federal Trade Commission decision to challenge their proposed $4 billion merger.
* An investment craze has surrounded the shares of companies who claim to have solutions to potential computer systems problems caused the coming of 2000.

* Market Place: Bankers Trust, in its just-announced aquisition of stock brokerage Alex Brown, is betting the health care and high technology industries will continue to prosper and need underwriters.
